summary: Hearing Mary’s report, Peter and the beloved disciple run to the tomb; they find the grave clothes left behind, and the other disciple sees and believes.
key_insight: The beloved disciple believed before he saw Jesus or heard an angel. What he saw was the linen cloths lying there and the head cloth folded in a place by itself. Thieves would have carried off the body in its wrappings, not unwrapped it and left the cloths behind.
story: Peter and the other disciple went out and headed for the tomb, both of them running. The other disciple outran Peter and came to the tomb first. Stooping down and looking in, he saw the linen cloths lying there, yet he did not go in. {Jn}

Then Simon Peter came after him. Stooping down, he saw the linen cloths lying by themselves, {Lk} and he went into the tomb. He saw the linen cloths lying there, and the handkerchief that had been around His head, “not lying with the linen cloths, but folded together in a place by itself.” {Jn}
Then the other disciple, who had reached the tomb first, went in too, “and he saw and believed.” For as yet they did not know the Scripture, that He must rise again from the dead. {Jn}
Then the disciples went back to their homes. {Jn} Peter went away marveling to himself at what had happened. {Lk}
differences: Luke tells only of Peter; John adds the other disciple and tells of their race to the tomb.
Luke says Peter stooped and looked in; John says the other disciple stooped and looked first, and Peter went inside.
Only John mentions the head cloth folded by itself and says the other disciple believed. Luke says Peter went away marveling.

fit.question: Luke mentions only Peter running to the tomb. John says Peter and “the other disciple” went together. Did one man go, or two?

points.label: Luke says so himself
points.text: Later in the same chapter, the two travelers to Emmaus tell Jesus, “certain of those who were with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said” (Luke 24:24). Luke knew more than one disciple went; in verse 12 he simply follows Peter.

fit.note: Luke’s own words settle it: he names Peter, and later says that more than one went.
fit.short: Luke follows Peter, but Luke 24:24 says “certain of those who were with us went to the tomb.”

scene.label: The grave clothes
scene.text: The body had been bound in strips of linen with about seventy-five pounds of myrrh and aloes (John 19:39–40). Wrappings laid with that much spice would have clung to the body. Yet the cloths lay there, and the body was gone.

scene.label: Lazarus and Jesus
scene.text: When Lazarus came out of his tomb, he was still bound hand and foot, with his face wrapped in a cloth, and others had to loose him (John 11:44). Jesus left His grave clothes behind.

scene.label: Stooping to look
scene.text: Rock tombs often had low entrances. To see inside, a person had to bend down, as the beloved disciple, Peter and later Mary all did (John 20:5, 11; Luke 24:12).

scene.label: “The Scripture”
scene.text: John does not say which Scripture he means. Peter later preached from Psalm 16:10, “Nor will You allow Your Holy One to see corruption,” as a promise of the resurrection (Acts 2:27, 31).

witnesses.luke: Luke gives one verse to Peter at the tomb: he stooped, saw the linen lying by itself and went home marveling. Later that day the disciples say the Lord “has appeared to Simon” (24:34), so Peter’s puzzled visit is the first step toward meeting the risen Lord.
witnesses.john: John tells the scene as one who was there, without naming himself: who ran faster, who went in first, how the head cloth lay. He admits that they did not yet understand the Scripture, and that his own belief that Jesus had risen began with what he saw in the empty tomb.

seeing.reveals: Jesus left death behind in order, not in haste. The empty linen and the folded cloth speak of a Lord who rose, not a body carried off by thieves.
seeing.living: The beloved disciple “saw and believed” before he understood the Scriptures; afterward the Scriptures confirmed what he had seen. Faith in the risen Christ rests on real events in a real tomb. Look honestly at what Jesus left behind, and let His word explain it.
seeing.ponder: Have you looked into the empty tomb long enough to believe?

preaching.big_idea: The empty grave clothes told the truth before anyone saw the risen Lord.
preaching.watch_for: John uses three different Greek verbs for “saw” in verses 5, 6 and 8, often explained as a glance from the doorway, a careful look, and seeing with understanding. The NKJV translates all three as “saw.”
